model_interpretation.claim: A two-sided recurrence anchored at exponent zero can eliminate powf calls entirely: powers on each side use at most 32 multiplications, rather than the parent's eight powf seeds and seven-step segments. Accumulating powers in double should limit rounding drift before conversion back to float for the unchanged payoff expression. Whether the added multiplications and double arithmetic improve full-call time, and whether near-boundary payoffs remain within tolerance, require controller measurements.

model_interpretation.claim: Reseeding a forward power recurrence every eight terminal indices should reduce powf calls from 64 to 8 per input while limiting each recurrence segment to at most seven multiplications. items.subject: Reduce terminal-state power-function cost without changing endpoint convention
items.objective: In `src/candidate.cpp`, focus only on generating terminal payoffs more cheaply than 64 repeated `powf` evaluations per input. Explore a recurrence or other general power-generation method while preserving all 64 terminal indices and their existing exponents `2*j-64` (`-64` through `62` by twos), the `max(0, X-S*upow)` floor, and the subsequent rollback. Validate varied inputs, especially values near payoff boundaries, against the fixed tolerance; record failed numerical variants and compare full-call timings.
